clue.text: Simple tart dressing in the field

parts.note: simple means basic, elementary
a tart is a promiscuous woman, slang slag in British English

explanation.surface: A plain pastry with a topping, served up out in a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: Basic slag is a by-product of steelmaking spread on fields as a phosphate fertiliser; 'dressing' is a farmer's word for such a top dressing, not salad dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: This steelworks by-product is spread over farmland as a fertilising top dressing.

clue.text: Instructions with strong cheese

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
F, forte, means strong or loud in music

explanation.surface: Directions for making something with pungent cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: A brief is a set of instructions, as given to a barrister or a designer.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrister's or designer's set of instructions for a job is called this.

clue.text: CE cowards put out doctrine of all-male clergy, say

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Church of England cowards are upset by a rule keeping priests male.
explanation.walkthrough: CE is the Church of England; its long refusal to ordain women is offered as an example of an unquestionable belief.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea held to be beyond criticism, like the rule of a men-only priesthood, is idiomatically called this.

clue.text: Where vehicles come to a standstill with no turning back

parts.note: cars are vehicles
to halt is to come to a standstill

indicators.note: turning back means the following word is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A spot where traffic stops dead and cannot reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the single word 'Where'; Carshalton is a suburb in south London.
explanation.definitionFit: A place-name: 'Where' asks for a location, and Carshalton is a district of south London.

clue.text: Greenery provides shelter in which to have a smoke

indicators.note: in which means the following pieces go inside the word for shelter

parts.note: lee means shelter, the side away from the wind
fag is British slang for a cigarette, a smoke

explanation.surface: Bushes give cover where you can sneak a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaves collectively make up a plant's foliage, which is greenery.

clue.text: Coat perhaps for man without a limb

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the word for man surrounds the limb

parts.note: gent, short for gentleman, means a man
an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: An overcoat for an amputee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking, but here it is the old sense outside, as in 'without the city walls'.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat is one example of an item of clothing, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Decline for which doctor finds nothing to work

parts.note: O, the figure zero, stands for nothing
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A slump in which the physician has no patients to treat.
explanation.definitionFit: To sag or flag is to decline in vigour, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Direction of Jones's partner before end of depression?

parts.note: the Dow Jones is the New York stock index, so Dow partners Jones

indicators.note: end of means take the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Which way does a stock index go before a slump ends?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at the stock market falling, which fits the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Downward is a direction, as opposed to up.

clue.text: It's clear from Dover to Calais

indicators.note: from means the answer is taken out of the following words

explanation.surface: Something plain to see when crossing the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run through 'dOVER To'; 'It's' joins the definition, and Calais completes the cross-Channel picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and plainly visible, a synonym of clear.

clue.text: Gymnastic qualifications reported lines of class evolution

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the sound of the words is what counts

parts.note: degrees in physical education, PE, would be gymnastic qualifications

explanation.surface: Accounts of sports-teacher diplomas tracing class development.
explanation.walkthrough: PE is physical education, school gym lessons; 'PE degrees' said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines of descent, recording how a breed or class developed, are called this.

clue.text: Bear incorporated old settlement

parts.note: INC is the abbreviation for incorporated, used after US company names
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia, birthplace of Abraham

explanation.surface: An animal that has been made into a company within an ancient town.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear costs or blame is to take them on, which is synonymous with this verb.

clue.text: Foremost in Fletcher's line of attack?

definitions.meaning: a fletcher makes arrows, and the part at the very front of his product is the pointed tip
a spearhead formation, a wedge leading an assault, is called by the same name

explanation.walkthrough: Fletcher looks like a surname, but a fletcher is a maker of arrows.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed tip leads an arrow's flight, so it is literally foremost in the archer's line of attack.

clue.text: Could it make ferret wash?

indicators.note: asks whether the letters of the following words could be rearranged into the answer, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Would some clean pond water get a ferret to bathe?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could it make' signals rearranging FERRET WASH; read whole, the clue also asks if water from a river could get a ferret clean.
explanation.definitionFit: Water from rivers and lakes, not salty, is what a ferret might bathe in.

clue.text: Game point short of level

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the point is taken away from the word for level

parts.note: a stage is a level or phase
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A tennis score just below deuce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game point' looks like tennis, but game is the definition: deer and other animals hunted for sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A male deer is a classic example of game, an animal hunted for sport.

clue.text: How to hold one's ground?

parts.note: not standing firm, but the legal terms on which a person occupies a piece of land

explanation.surface: How to stand firm against attack?
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom about standing firm means refusing to retreat; read literally, it is about owning land under some legal title.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal conditions under which land is held, as freehold or leasehold, are this term.

clue.text: Complicated clue for covering bad ball

indicators.note: covering means the rearranged clue wraps round the next piece
complicated means tangled, so the letters of clue are mixed up

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: A tricky crossword clue about hiding an awful delivery in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' is defined by its partner: Lucille Ball was the American comic actress of I Love Lucy. 'Complicated' gives LUCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The first name that goes with Ball, as in the comic actress Lucille Ball.

clue.text: Need for reading glasses in Manchester

definitions.meaning: being able to see far but not near makes a person need spectacles for reading
a district of Manchester, in north-west England, carries this name

explanation.definitionFit: Long-sightedness means poor near vision, and the same name is a district of Manchester.

clue.text: Model with a gait that makes no sense

parts.note: the Model T was Henry Ford's car, so model can give T
a waddle is a kind of gait, a duck-like walk

explanation.surface: A fashion model whose walk on the catwalk is baffling.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense is speech that makes no sense, and this word is a colloquial synonym for nonsense.

clue.text: Ten dismal components to take apart

indicators.note: components suggests the letters are parts to be reassembled in another order

explanation.surface: Ten dreary parts to break down.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle is to take a machine apart into its pieces, a direct synonym.

clue.text: No vintage wine here

parts.note: a wine with no vintage is new, not aged
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: A place where young wine is all they serve.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'here': the clue describes a place, and Newport is a town (several in Britain, and one in Rhode Island).
explanation.definitionFit: A place-name definition: 'here' points to a town, and Newport names several towns.

clue.text: Top liners weightlift in wood

indicators.note: in means the turned weight goes inside the word for wood

parts.note: a wood is made of trees
weight gives LB, pound, and lift turns it up in this down clue to read BL

explanation.surface: Star performers pump iron in the forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weightlift' splits: weight is LB (pound), lift reverses it upwards to BL. Trebles sing the top line in a choir.
explanation.definitionFit: Boy sopranos sing the highest part, the top line, in a choir.

clue.text: Ed and Cissy arranged removal of coat

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two friends set up a coat-check.
explanation.walkthrough: Ecdysis is the shedding of an outer skin by insects, snakes and crustaceans.
explanation.definitionFit: Moulting, when an animal sheds its outer skin or shell, is the technical term meant here.

clue.text: Account for one's involvement in abandoned scheme

parts.note: ex means former, given up or abandoned

indicators.note: involvement in means the one goes inside the following pieces

parts.note: a plan is a scheme
I, the Roman numeral, means one

explanation.surface: Justify your part in a project that was dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To account for something is to give reasons for it, which is a synonym.

clue.text: The Guardian turns on politician — there may be oil in it

definitions.text: there may be oil in it

indicators.note: turns means flipped around, so the letters for the paper are read backwards

parts.note: the Guardian, where the puzzle appears, can call itself us
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: The newspaper attacks a Member of Parliament in an oily affair.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter often refers to the paper as 'us', so The Guardian gives US, turned to SU.
explanation.definitionFit: A car engine's oil collects in this reservoir at the bottom of the crankcase.

clue.text: Stated method of provision in the desert

indicators.note: stated means said aloud, so the sound of the word counts

parts.note: manner means method, way of doing

explanation.surface: Way of supplying food in the wilderness, as described.
explanation.walkthrough: In Exodus, God fed the Israelites in the wilderness with bread from heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: The miraculous food the Israelites ate during their desert wanderings, in the Bible.

clue.text: Telegraph — garbled English communication system

indicators.note: garbled means jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A jumbled telegraph message in English.
explanation.walkthrough: Telpherage is an overhead cable transport system; the clue's 'communication' covers carrying things along a line.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerial cable system carrying loads, a dated sense of communication as a means of transport.

clue.text: Count on first year in good time

parts.note: an earl is the British counterpart of a continental count

indicators.note: first means take the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Rely on the first year arriving promptly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count on' looks like rely on, but Count is a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving ahead of the appointed time is being in good time, a synonym.

clue.text: Heads up — it's a knockout

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: nuts is slang for heads

explanation.surface: Warning to look out: a blow to the head is coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads up' looks like a warning, but heads is NUTS and up reverses it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock someone senseless, the effect of a knockout blow, is to daze them.

clue.text: Private parts information to EU country

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
Italia is Italy's own name for itself

explanation.surface: Confidential details passed to a European member state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private parts' reads as secret sections of a report, but means the sex organs.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain euphemism: private parts are the external sex organs.

clue.text: Speak what could be true — and about time!

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the next piece
what could be signals the letters of true in another possible arrangement

explanation.surface: Say something accurate, and not before time!
explanation.definitionFit: To utter words is to say or speak them, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Landscapes perhaps seen to go backwards in this

definitions.text: Landscapes perhaps seen to go backwards in this

parts.words: Landscapes perhaps seen to go backwards in this
parts.note: from a carriage window the countryside seems to slide past the other way as the vehicle moves along rails

explanation.surface: Scenery appears to run in reverse from this vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers on a railway see fields and hills appear to rush backwards past the window.

clue.text: Because trust is required, sign off with this

parts.note: since means because
to rely on is to trust

explanation.surface: A letter-writer chooses a closing word that inspires confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters addressed to a named person are traditionally closed with 'Yours' and this adverb.
